1.explanation:
• ComboBox/index.js — entry point that wires up props (including itemToString) to the component.
• ComboBox/ComboBox.js — contains the downshift integration and default itemToString implementation.
• ComboBox/ListBoxMenu.js — maps items to MenuItem elements and assigns the React key.
• ComboBox/MenuItem.js — defines how each option is rendered and where the key prop is applied.
• ComboBox/tools — any examples or test fixtures showing how items are passed in and rendered.
• ListBox/README.md — describes the ListBox basis for menu rendering so you understand the underlying pattern and key usage.

Together, these files show where keys are derived, how items flow through the component, and are the starting points to change the key from item.text to item.id so that duplicate-text options no longer collide.
1.bug_scenario: In the provided screenshot and code sandbox, a ComboBox is rendered with two items that share the same text (“Option”) but have different IDs. Because ComboBox uses the result of itemToString(item) (i.e. item.text) as the React key on each MenuItem, React complains about duplicate keys. In the dropdown list you can see two entries labeled “Option,” and in the console you see the “Encountered two children with the same key, `Option`” warning. The root cause is that MenuItem keys are generated from the visible text rather than the unique id.
